text.p: Following are the highlights of the main stories in the Bosnian press on Tuesday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Council of Ministers is due to resume discussion on citizenship and passport laws on Tuesday. Council co-chairman, Haris Silajdzic, said a Serb request that entities decide on granting citizenship is unacceptable.

- Silajdzic and the Croat member of the council, Neven Tomic, signed on Monday a memorandum of understanding on opening civilian airports in Tuzla, Mostar and Banja Luka. The Serb member, Boro Bosic, refused to sign the agreement.

- Silajdzic says that a proposal on distributing ambassadorial posts from the office of the High Representative violates minority rights by excluding a national or religious category for "others" not belonging to Moslem, Croat or Serb communities.
- The chairman of Bosnia's collective presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, signed on Monday an order forming a commission to investigate alleged misuse of international aid funds.
- Head of the Mostar branch of the Croatian Democratic Unity (HDZ), Mile Puljic, says that Mostar is and will remain a Croat town.

- Central bank deputy governer Obrad Piljak says the privatization process is the only way that people can get back their old bank savings because banks currently lack funds to pay for the savings. Bosnian banks owe 3.4 billion German marks ($1.9).

- The president and vice-president of the Moslem-Croat federation, Vladimir Soljic and Ejup Ganic, said an incident in which Moslems were attacked in Jajce was meant to damage Croat-Moslem relations before a meeting between Izetbegovic and Croatian President Franjo Tudjman.
- Telephone links between the federation and the Serb entity were restored on Monday at midnight, the telephone company said

- The Moslem Party of Democratic Action (SDA) in Capljina requests that voter registration in Capljina be cancelled due to abuses by the Croatian Democratic Unity (HDZ). The SDA accused the HDZ of inflating the number of Croat voters in Capljina by 5,000.
